experiment: leave-one-generator-out on the eta=0 (scheme C) features
question: is scheme C's family bias a training artefact (sdv1.4-only training) or a property of the feature itself?
protocol: classifier trained on five generators' test-half features (first half of each class, 30k total), evaluated on the sixth generator it never saw; same architecture and hyperparameters as every other run
observations: held-out accuracy is chance for every generator (48.0-53.4%), so training diversity does not create transfer
validation accuracy on the five TRAINED generators is also only 51.8-58.2% -- mixing generators destroys even the in-domain fit that single-family training had

wukong (SD-family) drops from 78.5% under sdv1.4-only training to 50.4% when the five non-SD generators form the training set: the SD signal must come from SD-family training data, not from other generators
conclusion: the family bias is a property of the eta=0 feature (it encodes how well the SD1.4 inverter round-trips the image), not an artefact of the original training composition
